### Specify which documentation you found a problem with

docs/SECURITY.md, docs/CODE_REVIEW.md, README.md (top-level)

### The problem

Audit of three curl process docs (docs/SECURITY.md, docs/CODE_REVIEW.md, README.md).

Findings:

1. SECURITY.md -- disclosure policy is declarative, not operational (critical)
2. CODE_REVIEW.md -- no mandatory security review for sensitive PRs (critical)
3. README.md -- missing examples and security-contact pointer (important)

Details below.

---

## Finding 1: SECURITY.md -- disclosure policy is declarative, not operational (critical)

### What the doc says

SECURITY.md is short. It links to VULN-DISCLOSURE-POLICY.md, points to
a web form at curl.se/dev/vuln-disclosure.html, and mentions OpenSSF
Gold status. It is a declarative document.

### What's missing

1. No SLA. A researcher does not know when to expect acknowledgment,
   triage, or fix. Industry standard: ack in 48h, triage in 7 days.
2. No severity classification. CVSS is not mentioned. Without it,
   triage priority is unclear -- a critical RCE and a minor info leak
   may be processed the same way.
3. No fallback channel. The only reporting path is the web form. If
   the form is down, blocked by a corporate firewall, or unavailable
   to a researcher in a restricted network, there is no way to report.
   Most projects offer security@... + PGP key.
4. No embargo policy. No defined window between report and public
   disclosure. Common source of friction: researchers may
   full-disclose out of frustration.
5. No safe harbor. A good-faith researcher may worry about legal
   consequences.

### Real-world precedent

- OpenSSL publishes a security policy with SLA and channels.
- Linux kernel has Documentation/process/security-bugs.rst with a
  clear process, embargo, and multiple channels.
- XZ Utils post-mortem shows that single-channel processes can fail
  at critical moments.

### Proposed fix (Option A, 2-3 days)

Add to SECURITY.md:

1. SLA table:
   - Acknowledgment: <= 48h
   - Triage: <= 7 days
   - Fix: by severity (critical: <= 30 days; high: <= 90; etc.)
2. Fallback channel: security@curl.se + public PGP fingerprint.
3. Severity classification: reference CVSS v4.0.
4. Embargo window: 90 days (industry standard).
5. Safe harbor statement for good-faith researchers.

Documentation-only, no code changes.

---

## Finding 2: CODE_REVIEW.md -- no mandatory security review (critical)

### What the doc covers

CODE_REVIEW.md covers style, formatting, naming, memory management,
thread-safety, portability, types, overflow handling, test and
documentation requirements, and interpersonal aspects ("be nice",
language barriers, first-timers). This is a strong technical guide,
with one line mentioning "sensitive data".

### What's missing

1. No mandatory security review. A PR touching TLS, authentication,
   protocol parsing, or credentials can be merged by a reviewer
   without security expertise, as long as style and tests look good.
2. No ABI-diff in CI. Breaking changes to libcurl's ABI can be merged
   without automated detection. Downstream users discover the break
   only at integration time.
3. No SLA / metrics. Review can stall indefinitely. No published
   metric of time-to-first-review or time-to-merge.
4. No rollback process. Once merged, code goes into next release
   without a defined rollback procedure.

### Why this is critical for curl specifically

- libcurl is a shared library; ABI breaks are breaking changes for
  all downstream.
- curl handles TLS and auth; a subtle security bug is not always
  caught by tests.
- OpenSSL and Rust RFC process have formal checklists for this;
  curl's doc stops short.

### Proposed fix (Option A, 2-3 days)

Add to CODE_REVIEW.md:

1. Mandatory security checklist for PRs labeled "security":
   - TLS: verify verification is on, no --insecure-like defaults.
   - Auth: no credentials in logs, no weak defaults.
   - Parsing: fuzz-relevant changes require fuzz tests.
   - Credentials: no new logging of secrets.
2. Assign a security contact for security PRs.
3. abidiff / abipkgdiff in CI. Merge is blocked if ABI changes are
   not declared in the PR description.
4. TSAN run for PRs touching shared state.

---

## Finding 3: README.md -- missing examples and security-contact pointer (important)

### What the doc says

README.md is around 60 lines. It contains project identity, protocol
list, install pointers, libcurl pointer, community/support links,
security section, funding.

### What's missing

1. No command examples. A first-time user cannot see how to use curl
   at a glance. Competing tools (wget, httpie) show examples in
   README.
2. Security contact is not prominent. The security section links to
   SECURITY.md, but there is no security@ email or PGP fingerprint in
   README itself.
3. No warning for -k / --insecure. Users can easily learn the "just
   add -k" workaround without seeing a warning.
4. No warning for -o / -O overwrite. Users can overwrite files by
   accident.

### Proposed fix

1. Add 3-5 command examples (GET, POST, download, upload).
2. Move security-contact pointer up + include email/PGP.
3. Add warning near first example: "do not use -k in production".
4. Add warning for -o / -O: "silently overwrites files".

---

## Summary of severity

| Finding | Severity | Fix cost | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| SECURITY.md -- no SLA/channels/embargo | critical | 2-3 days | single channel; lost reports |
| CODE_REVIEW.md -- no security review | critical | 2-3 days | missed CVEs, ABI breaks |
| README.md -- no examples/contact | important | 1 day | onboarding friction; -k misuse |

---

## How this audit was produced

The three docs were analyzed by Vishap (LLM-based analyzer) on
2026-10-16. Vishap's pipeline detected 11 risk nodes and 8 threats
across these files.
